explain.1: Load json: it turns text into lists and dictionaries, and back. MCP and A2A messages are JSON.
explain.4: A made-up order sheet: order number → what it is and where it's at.
explain.6: The tool itself: a plain function. It takes its arguments as a dictionary.
explain.7: Look up the order number. If it isn't there, say so.
explain.9: The MCP server: its list of tools (name, description, inputs) and the functions that run them.
explain.19: Define tools/list: the server's answer when a client asks what tools it has.
explain.20: The answer, in MCP's shape: a JSON-RPC message whose result is the list of tools.
explain.23: Define describe: the client turns the tool list into lines for a bot's instructions.
explain.24: Start an empty list of lines.
explain.25: Ask the server for its tools, and go through them one by one.
explain.26: The inputs this tool needs, joined with commas (here just order_id).
explain.27: One line per tool: its name, what it needs, and what it does.
explain.28: Glue all the lines together into one text, one per line, and hand it back.
explain.30: Show the lines a bot would get in its instructions.
explain.33: Define tools/call: the server runs one tool, or answers with an error.
explain.35: The arguments for it, as a dictionary.
explain.38: Is this the one asked for?
explain.41: Send back an error: no tool with that name.
explain.42: Go through every input this tool needs.
explain.43: Is one missing from the arguments?
explain.44: Send back an error that names the missing input.
explain.45: All good: run the tool's function with the arguments.
explain.46: Send back the result, in MCP's shape: content, as text.
explain.49: Define handle: what the program does with a bot's CALL line.
explain.50: Try the next line. If it goes wrong, jump to except instead of crashing.
explain.51: Remove “CALL ” and read the rest as JSON: a dictionary with name and arguments.
explain.53: Send back an error the bot can read and fix.
explain.54: Wrap it as an MCP request: method tools/call, with the bot's name and arguments.
explain.55: Send it to the server and get its reply.
explain.56: Did the server send back an error?
explain.57: Pass the error on to the bot, as text.
explain.61: A bad call: the input is named id, not order_id. The server says what's missing.
explain.64: A made-up courier's Agent Card: its name, its address, and its skills.
explain.67: Read the card: who it is and what it can do.
explain.70: Define send_task: give another company's agent a job, and follow its status.
explain.71: The task starts as submitted: sent, not started.
explain.73: The courier's agent reports back: first working, then completed.
explain.76: The finished task carries its result.
explain.79: Send the courier's agent a task, in plain words.
